title: Chromosome mutations and polyploidy; Types of selection; Natural selection
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EV01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV01a#t4 term and clue written for the game; EV01a#t3 term and clue written for the game; GE07#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EV01a#N.2, GE07#N.6a, EV01a#N.6a, GE07#N.10, EV01a#N.8a, EV01a#N.11, EV01a#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mutation
items.clue: The original source of all new alleles; it arises at random

items.label: Evolution
items.clue: A change in the allele frequencies of a population over time

items.label: Fitness
items.clue: Reproductive success: leaving surviving offspring that go on to breed

items.label: Non-disjunction
items.clue: Failure of a pair to separate in meiosis, so both go to the same pole.

questions.stem: A population of a plant species has two alleles of a flower-colour gene. A third allele, never seen before, appears in one seedling. Which process could have produced it?

options.text: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes in meiosis in one of the parents
Random fertilisation, when an unusual combination of two gametes came together
A mutation in a cell that went on to form a gamete in one of the parents
The plant producing the allele because a new colour would help it attract pollinators

questions.explanation: Only mutation makes new alleles. To appear in a seedling, it must have arisen in a cell that formed a gamete.

questions.stem: A child has Down syndrome. Both parents have 46 chromosomes in each of their body cells. Which statement about the origin of the condition in this child is correct?

options.text: A mutation in the zygote altered the base sequence of one gene on chromosome 21, so the child carries a faulty allele of that gene.
The extra chromosome 21 was produced at fertilisation, when the nuclei of a normal sperm and a normal egg fused and their chromosomes combined.
One parent produced a gamete with 24 chromosomes because chromosome 21 failed to separate in meiosis, so the zygote had 47 chromosomes.
One parent's meiosis gave a gamete two copies of chromosome 21, and every other gamete from that division had the normal number of 23.

questions.stem: In a population of red deer, stag X is the largest and strongest male but leaves two offspring that survive to breed. Stag Y is smaller and weaker but leaves six offspring that survive to breed. Which stag has the higher fitness, and why?

options.text: Stag X, because fitness means the physical strength and bodily condition of the individual animal
Stag X, because natural selection favours traits that aid survival rather than reproduction
Neither, because fitness is a property of the deer species as a whole and not of individuals
Stag Y, because fitness is measured by the number of surviving offspring a genotype contributes

questions.stem: In a hypothetical animal, a segment carrying several genes breaks off one copy of chromosome 4 and is lost, while the rest of that chromosome remains in the cell. Which statement best explains why this change can lead to a genetic disorder?

options.text: The cell has lost a whole copy of chromosome 4, so every gene on that chromosome is now missing
Each gene in the segment now has a point mutation, which can change the protein it codes for
Each gene in the lost segment is left with one copy, which can alter the amount of its product
Every gene after the break point on chromosome 4 is now read in a shifted reading frame

questions.stem: A woman develops large, strong arm muscles through years of rowing training. Will her children inherit larger arm muscles as a result of her training?

options.text: Yes, because characteristics that an individual acquires during life are passed on to its offspring
Yes, if she teaches her children to row, because anything passed from parent to child is heritable
No, because muscle growth caused by training is not encoded in the base sequence of her genes
Yes, because the training causes mutations in the genes for muscle growth that her children will receive

questions.stem: A population of 50 plants contains 8 RR, 24 Rr and 18 rr. What is the frequency of allele R?
questions.explanation: 50 plants carry 100 alleles. R = 2 × 8 + 24 = 40, so its frequency is 40 ÷ 100 = 0.40.

questions.stem: A student builds a flowchart model of how natural selection increased the mean beak depth of a population of a hypothetical seed-eating bird species over several generations of drought. Which flowchart best represents this process?

options.text: Birds vary in heritable beak depth → seeds are scarce → deep-beaked birds leave more offspring → mean beak depth rises
Birds crack hard seeds → their beaks deepen with use → their offspring inherit the deeper beaks → mean beak depth rises
Birds vary in beak depth → seeds are scarce → each bird's beak deepens over its life → mean beak depth rises
Drought begins → the drought causes new deep-beaked variants to arise → these birds then survive → mean beak depth rises
